summary: Martin Schwartz works in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under Walter Bruno Henning and was attested as a Professor of the Department of Near Eastern Studies at the University of California, Berkeley in 2000.

Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2004 under Barend Jan Terwiel. He held a post at Hamburg in 2004 and is attested as a Council Member at the Pali Text Society in 2026.

Martin Straube specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies and studied under Michael Hahn. His positions include roles at the University of Marburg, the Pali Text Society, and 2026 appointments at Göttingen Academy, Bristol, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and IIBS.

Martin T. Adam specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes, studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and under several teachers including Ashok Aklujkar, and taught as an instructor at McGill.

Martin Williams worked in Indology and religious studies, completing an MA at Keele University (1972-1979). He served as an IT Adviser for Powys County Council (1989-2007) and Co-ordinator of the Naga Conciliation Group for the Religious Society of Friends (2011-2014).

Martin Willson (d. 2005) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under several traditional teachers, including Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna and was supervised by Lambert Schmithausen for her MA. She served as Numata Professor at the University of Vienna (2021) and McGill University (2022).

Martina Palladino specializes in Indology and religious studies, earning degrees from the University of Bologna and SOAS University of London. She has held posts as an Adjunct Professor at the University of Bologna and a postdoc researcher at Ghent University (2023).

Martine Kropman is an Indologist who conducted PhD research at the University of Groningen and is attested in 2026 as a PhD candidate at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Peter C. Bisschop.
Martino Dibeltulo specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed a PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and was mentored by Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg (1922-2016) was an art historian who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939-1943) and Princeton University (~1946-1954). He served on the faculty at the University of Michigan from circa 1949 to 1988.
Mary Anne Cartelli works in sinology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University, attested in 1999, under the supervision of Philip Boas Yampolsky.

Mary Belle Harris (1874-1957) was an Indology scholar who earned an A.B. from Bucknell University, a Ph.D. in Sanskrit from the University of Chicago (~1897-1900), and also studied at Johns Hopkins. She taught at the American School of Classical Studies in Rome (1912-1914).

Mary Boyce (1920-2006) specialized in Iranian studies and religious studies, completing a PhD at SOAS under Walter Bruno Henning. She held academic posts at SOAS from 1947, becoming Professor of Iranian Studies (1963-1982), and was an Honorary Fellow at AIIT.

Mary Brockington is an Indologist who has served as a Research Fellow at the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (attested 2016-2020) and as a Fellow at the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (attested 2018-2020).

Mary Cecilia Foley (1859-1925) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a B.Sc. from University College London in 1891. She served as Chief Lady Invigilator at the University of London from 1901 to 1925.

Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917-1970) was a historian and sinologist educated at Vassar College and Radcliffe College (PhD ~1951). She worked as curator of the China collection at Stanford (1947) and became a professor at Yale University (1959-1970).

Mary Evelyn Tucker is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and japanology who earned degrees from SUNY Fredonia, Columbia (PhD), and UCLA. She has held posts at Bucknell (~1989-2005), Harvard, UC Berkeley, and Yale University (attested ~2006).

Mary Haas (1910-1996) was a linguist who studied under Edward Sapir at the University of Chicago and Yale University (~1931-1935). She served on the faculty of the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1943 to 1977.

Mary Jaksch is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland as a student of Peter Harvey (attested 2007) and trained under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.
